interrupt_contract.vector: IM 1 $0038: DI / PUSH AF / IN A,($BF) / RLCA / JP C,$04E2 (vblank) else JP $0650 (line interrupt, no mapper access)
interrupt_contract.irq_exit_contract: every RET reached from the vector, with callees treated as opaque and every register store other than LD A,(shadow) / LD ($FFFF),A treated as a change, leaves $FFFF equal to the shadow
interrupt_contract.exit_restoration: LD A,($D12A) / LD ($FFFE),A at $0607; LD A,($D12B) / LD ($FFFF),A at $060D; both rewrite the registers from their RAM shadows immediately before POP/EI/RET

restart_paths.rule: a JP to $0450 (DI / LD SP) discards the interrupted context; the walk does not follow it

zone_music_table.index: L = 3*$D297 + $D298 (8-bit), so bytes past the 39th are code bytes unless zone and act are bounded

script_operand_route.rule: the handler reads the byte after the FF 06 pair, so a forbidden id needs FF 06 followed by it in the ROM

clamp.stored_range: $80-$C4 and $FF: CP $FF / JP Z; CP $C5 / JP C store; $C5 -> $FF, above -> $C4

sound_test.conclusion: open: the loop's closure contains unresolved computed jumps, so a store to $D2BF outside $0B38/$0BCC cannot be excluded

record_table.record_fetch_requires: zone $D297 <= 15 and act $D298 <= 2 when the level loader runs

allocator.other_ways_to_reach_the_vector: the 16-bit value $0374 also occurs as data; callback stubs can enter it with whatever C the caller holds, so its C values are not enumerated

lemmas_that_would_discharge_it: ZONE/ACT: whenever $18A0 runs, 3*$D297+$D298 <= 38 (otherwise the music-table read at $18B2 continues into code bytes from $18E1, which include request bytes in $C5-$D3)
SOUND TEST: $D2BF changes only at $0B38 and $0BCC while the sound-test loop runs (its closure has unresolved computed jumps, so stores at the other writers are not excluded)
RECORD FETCH: $D297 <= 15 and $D298 <= 2 whenever the level loader at $2A4F runs, so the four slot types come from the nine records (types 0-14)
ALLOCATOR: every caller of $1CD3 passes C <= 20; only the direct call sites (C = 7, 9, 16) are enumerated, the kernel vector $0374 can also be entered through callback stubs with an unknown C
ZONE TYPE: while a slot of type 5 runs, $D297 <= 5 (type 5 occurs only in the records of zones 2, 4 and 5)

residual_assumptions.text: Interrupt preservation of the slot-2 mapper register and its shadow $D12B across the handler's banked callees. See verdict for the state after DECOMP-1D-R1.

Register-addressed stores ((HL), (DE), (BC), (IX+d), (IY+d), block moves) that could alias $FFFC-$FFFF or the shadow or its RAM mirror are not modelled. Absolute stores are, in every encoding, including the mirror; register-addressed stores are only counted and classified.

Slot 1 is bank 1 whenever the IM 1 handler starts (unchanged from DECOMP-1D). The dispatchers resolved here assume the handler's own mappings (slot 1 = bank 2, slot 2 = bank 3 for the sound driver; slot 2 = bank $1D for the routine at $8000).
Standard Sega mapper semantics, corroborated only by the ROM's own register use; no emulator or hardware trace.

The instruction universe is the code discovered by the reset/IM 1/NMI walk, the recovered regions and the resolved dispatchers. Entry-integrity proofs hold against that universe; operand-position 16-bit literals in bytes no evidence classifies are listed per proof and are not shown inert.

Stack discipline: RET is treated as returning to the caller. Handlers that deliberately unwind (POP HL / POP HL / RET) return to a caller the walk also reaches; the walk does not model stack contents.

ledger_effect.note: No recovered region, seed or classification is added; the deferred DECOMP-1D regions stay deferred for Manager review.
